Round 7 is done in the working tree, text only, and nothing is committed. src/ and tests/ are byte for byte shift-r6's, and the 76 S-PAR-02 files all pass `sha1sum -c`. The quick suite passes: 720 tests in 27.06 s at a median of 15 % load.

**One change to the ruling's sentence.** Before writing, I read the code. `MassProps.ownership` orders overlaps by kept parts first, then the slot's rank (§3.7), then `Sampling.measureRanked`. That last one puts a cleaned part's material first and the slot's name late (Grip before Guard). So the ruling's phrase 'later in the measure's rank (§4.4)' gives wrong answers across slots. I measured three such cases on round 6 and f7ac37d (work\rankslot.luau):
- An Iron copy of a hidden Steel part in a lower-ranked slot changes nothing.
- A Steel copy of an Iron filler in the Blade takes its place (+2.1 g).
- A copy of filler 17 in the Grip changes nothing.

I kept every other word of the canonical sentence and changed only that phrase, to 'the priority above (kept parts, then slot rank, then the measure's rank of §4.4)'. Elsewhere it reads '§4.3's priority'. All 26 measured cases agree with it, including 16 kept-part cases in work\keptcopy.luau. This is reported as a deviation for the lead to confirm.

**Where the rule now appears.** It is stated in full in §4.3, §17.2's hidden-parts row and E-S2.14's item (1), the last with labelled examples. §5.6's hidden-cores row and README carry it with parentheses dropped, and the plain words in plain words.
